task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR within a possession
methodological_questions: Can DRIVE and PNR be labeled reliably enough from play-by-play to define exposure and outcome?
Is any PPP difference causal or confounded by lineup, opponent, game state and possession context?
Are the exposure and the outcome produced by the same labeling process, so that label artifacts could create the effect?
Are there enough drive-then-PNR possessions to detect a plausible effect, and how should multiplicity be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type label backfill verification FAILED overall. PNR share was 28.7% (expected band 20-28%), 3100 games had team PNR share above 33%, team identity failed, and 2024-25 PULL_UP share was about 0-2% for many teams. PNR PPP of 0.948 passed. 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. Recorded failure mechanism: C_artifact, limited by label or classification error. Sample was 921,514 possessions.

Labeling audit found OTHER PPP inflated by 36% foul endings, DRIVE 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK), and PNR with a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict: artifact_found.

Inferred-label analysis of defensive scheme change could not separate a real effect from label noise. Near-uniform transition matrices were consistent with label noise. Recorded failure mechanism: A_unanswerable, limited by label or classification error.
On-ball coverage labels from matchup/PBP fields reached only 14.9% and 3.3% confident label rates in the ORL-DET G1 sample. switches_on was not populated. Verdict: failed_gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilled play-type labels (including PNR and DRIVE or PULL_UP) as a validated basis for analysis
failed_approaches.why: Label or classification error: share bands were violated, team identity failed, and 2024-25 PULL_UP was near zero. Recorded as a C_artifact mechanism.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing PPP across play-type labels, including DRIVE and PNR, at face value
failed_approaches.why: Foul-ending leakage inflates or deflates PPP by label (DRIVE 12pp below the foul benchmark, PNR 22% foul rate). Labels map to real play types for only 0.7% of possessions via initiation_type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred labels to detect sequential changes between play types
failed_approaches.why: Inferred labels cannot separate a real effect from label noise or from the offense executing differently.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball coverage from matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Very low confident-label rates, small sample, and an unpopulated switches_on field.

evidence_establishes: As recorded in [prior work][prior work], the derived play-type labels failed verification, and the 2024-25 DRIVE/PULL_UP labeling was suspect.
As recorded in [prior work][prior work], PPP by play-type label is contaminated by foul-ending leakage, and DRIVE and PNR are both affected.
Records on inferred labels ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) show that findings based on them were untestable because of label noise.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate drive before a PNR raises PNR PPP: no retrieved record tests this question directly.
Whether DRIVE can be identified reliably from raw play-by-play fields (shot distance, action type) independently of the derived labels.
The size of the drive-then-PNR sample.
Whether the label problems were fixed after these studies. No retrieved record shows a fix.
own_inferences: Any naive comparison of PNR PPP with versus without a preceding DRIVE would likely reflect label artifacts and selection, not a causal effect.
A preceding DRIVE is probably an endogenous marker of a broken defense or of the possession's flow. This confounds PPP even if labels were perfect.
The phrase 'any teammate DRIVE' is vague. It does not say how close in time the drive must be, or whether the drive can be the same possession or the same sequence.
Foul-ending leakage probably also affects the drive-first PNR possessions differently, biasing PPP in an unknown direction.
A minimum viable test is possible only after an independent label validation gate is passed.
uncertainties: [prior work] [prior work][prior work], cited as related, was not available (read_family returned an error), so its content is unknown.
The number of qualifying drive-then-PNR possessions is unknown, and so is the plausible effect size.
The status of label fixes after the recorded audits is unknown.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13 and the playoffs from 2026-06-21. The question date is 2026-06-14, so playoff data are partial and the final dataset is not yet fixed.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the question would look testable with a possession-level regression. The retrieved records show that derived DRIVE and PNR labels failed verification, that PPP by label is contaminated by foul leakage, and that inferred-label analyses were untestable. This moved the decision from proceeding to proceed_with_changes: the test is gated on independent label validation and a restricted, rebuilt exposure definition. If the gate fails, the question should not proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: Derived DRIVE and PNR labels failed verification ([prior work][prior work]). 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated and 2024-25 PULL_UP/DRIVE labeling was suspect.
Exposure (DRIVE) and outcome (PNR PPP) come from the same label-generating process and play-by-play outcomes, so artifacts can create or hide an effect ([prior work][prior work]).
A preceding drive correlates with a collapsed defense, lineup quality and possession context.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether a drive before a PNR changes PNR PPP. The retrieved records only show that the labels needed for such a test have documented quality and artifact problems.

risks.text: DRIVE and PNR misclassification, with season-specific failures such as 2024-25 DRIVE/PULL_UP shares near zero.
Play types and their PPP are derived from the same play-by-play. Possessions ending in a drive-related foul or shot may be labeled in ways that depend on the outcome.
Lineup quality, opponent, score and clock state, ball-handler identity, and possession time elapsed all affect both a drive and the PNR outcome.
Drive-then-PNR sequences within one possession may be rare after strict label filtering.
PPP has a high variance per possession (about 1.2 points SD), so detecting small differences needs thousands of possessions per arm.
Foul-ending leakage (PNR 22% foul rate, DRIVE below the foul benchmark) creates mechanical PPP differences by label.
Labeling quality and play style vary across 2022-23 to 2025-26, and the playoff data are partial.
Many possible definitions of 'any' teammate drive (window, player, lineup) invite forking paths.
Windows defined from the full possession record could use information from after the PNR started.

design.estimand: Within-possession difference in PNR PPP (points per possession, with fouls handled explicitly) between PNR possessions preceded by a teammate DRIVE within a fixed window (for example 8 seconds before the screen) and matched PNR possessions without such a drive, adjusted for context. This is an associational estimate with a causal-interpretation caveat.
design.unit: PNR possession (or PNR action sequence within a possession), clustered by game and by team-season.
design.sample: Regular-season PNR possessions from the three complete seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25, plus the complete 2025-26 regular season (use only after 2026-04-13). Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs from the confirmatory test because they are incomplete before 2026-06-21; use them as a holdout once complete. Require both drive and PNR to be independently identified from raw play-by-play fields (shot distance, action type, clock) with a manual audit of at least 300 sampled possessions per season. Exclude seasons failing the audit gate (precision below 90% for either label). Exclude garbage time.
design.power: Compute the exposed count first, before looking at outcomes. With PPP SD of about 1.2, detecting a 0.05 PPP difference at 80% power and alpha 0.05 needs about 9,000 possessions per arm. If the exposed arm is under about 3,000, the test is declared underpowered and only an effect size with a confidence interval is reported. Do not claim a null.
design.controls: Matched or regression adjustment for offense and defense team strength, lineup, ball handler and screener identity, score margin, period and clock, seconds elapsed in the possession, home/away, and season. Cluster-robust standard errors at the game level. Foul-ending handled by reporting PPP including and excluding free-throw trips, or by using expected points for fouls. Hold the label process constant across both arms.
design.falsification: Placebo exposures: a teammate drive after the PNR, a drive in the previous possession, and random-window shifts, each of which should give no effect. Also compare a non-drive action (for example a pass or cut) before the PNR. Negative-control seasons and teams where the label audit failed should show artifact patterns. Label-shuffle permutation test within game.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary test (any drive within the 8-second window, pooled seasons with season fixed effects). Secondary analyses (window length 5/12 seconds, drive by ball handler type, by season) are labeled exploratory and adjusted with Holm correction across the family.
design.decision_rule: Gate 1: the label audit passes (precision of at least 90% for both labels in each included season), otherwise do_not_proceed with a record of untestable. Gate 2: the exposed sample reaches the power threshold. Supported if the primary effect is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero, the placebos are null, and the sign is stable across at least three of four seasons and across the foul-handling variants. Rejected only if the CI excludes effects of at least +0.05 PPP at adequate power. Otherwise report inconclusive.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived play-type graph records as available on 2026-06-14. Freeze the extraction hash and the label version before analysis. 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13. 2025-26 playoffs are partial until 2026-06-21 and reserved as a holdout. Record the label backfill version, since [prior work][prior work] indicates a failed backfill.
